label: road E->W 7 the threshing floor to the grove
why: the road across the threshing floor's south half (bench 358.3/13.6 north of it) to the pale grove, west of the charcoal train's lane. (the same stretch reversed)

label: road W->E 8 down to the small bridge and over it to its east end
why: the charcoal train walks S1.road.main's last 15 m (paths X 370.5-384.9, D 10.9-15.7) between the pool north of the bridge and the bank, so the end-to-end walk leaves the road at the grove and takes the path over the small bridge (S1.road.path_36380) to the bridge's east end, 1 m clear of the train's lane. (Run 3, the S1 finisher: down the bank to the path's start (366.2, 10.0), then the bridge walk's legs; the shore land is now held 0.7 m over the water 2.5 m in, so the east landing stands at H -0.33)

label: road E->W 8 down to the small bridge and over it to its east end
why: the charcoal train walks S1.road.main's last 15 m (paths X 370.5-384.9, D 10.9-15.7) between the pool north of the bridge and the bank, so the end-to-end walk leaves the road at the grove and takes the path over the small bridge (S1.road.path_36380) to the bridge's east end, 1 m clear of the train's lane. (the same stretch reversed) (Run 3, the S1 finisher: off the deck along its north half (the south half of the west landing drops into a 0.3 m hollow with a 35 deg face, see notes), then north up the bank to the grove)

label: the nine trees in the road strip, close, W->E: up into each gap a walker fits and round each cluster
why: trunk colliders r = 0.3 x scale (0.26-0.41 m) + the walker's 0.3: the gaps 33433|33785 (4.2 m), 33936|34030 (1.4 m, 0.14 m clear: not taken), 34030|34110 (1.2 m) and 34110|34552 (5.3 m) fit; 33785-33936 and 34552-34703 (0.5-1.1 m) don't: round them on the yard bank's face (top D 11.8-12.0). Must not get stuck; a drift down the bank face is reported, not failed.

label: the nine trees in the road strip, close, E->W
why: the same weave from the east.

label: the willow dyke (S1.grd.bank_31660) W->E along its top among the great willows
why: the dyke's top (between bank_31660's top, D 3.0-3.2, and the yard / willow banks' feet, D 4.4-5.4): south of willow_great_31620 / 31715 (D 4.4-4.5), north round willow_great_31910 (309.65, 3.5), then east to the bank behind the massive willows.

label: the willow dyke E->W along its top
why: the same line reversed.

label: up the willow dyke's face from the road (north, square to the bank)
why: bank_31660 foot D 2.15 -> top D 3.15 at X 305: the rise is the builder's choice (recorded); it must be walkable: with 0.8 s more held the walker ends on the top (D >= 3.4, before the shed yard's bank at D 5.2), never stuck on the face. (Run 3, the S1 finisher: the ground agent's last build carries the dyke's crest at about H 0.07 (the road below it about -0.5); the walker climbs it at 1 s and is never stuck on the face)

label: down the willow dyke's face to the road (south)
why: and back down, stopping on the road (bank_31680 drops again at D 1.3).

label: up the hut's bank (S1.grd.bank_30750) from the road's bend, north to the farmhouse wing's east end
why: bank_30750 foot D 3.6-3.9 -> top D 4.6-4.9 at X 292.5; ends 0.9 m east of the wing's corner (291.6, 7.8) and 2.5 m short of the hall (D 9.1): on the top, not stuck on the face.

label: down the hut's bank to the travellers' path
why: the same bank down, ending north of the travellers' moving donkeys (D <= 1.0 here).

label: up the yard bank (S1.grd.yard_bank_34400) to the barn's front, east of the hedge
why: yard bank foot D 11.0 -> top D 11.8 at X 356, then the barn's open front (D 13.3-13.5): the fence and hedge end at X 353.6, so the bank top is reachable here (on the top, D >= 11.9).

label: down the yard bank to the terrace
why: and down again onto the terrace below the farmsteads.

label: across the 菜地 (S1.grd.field_vegetable_29790, a raised bed with its 14 saplings), W->E
why: the field's footprint X 279.7-288.2, D 4.2-8.5: the saplings are under 3 m (no trunk collider); the bed's rim must be walkable both ways (the climb onto the bed slows you: the box runs 1 m short).

label: across the 菜地 E->W
why: and back, up onto the bed from the east.

label: across the threshing floor (S1.grd.threshing_floor_35225) W->E along its south half
why: the floor's footprint X 356.2-362.9, D 12.4-14.9; south of the bench (358.3, 13.35 after its recorded move) and the posts (358.2-358.6, 13.6-14.3). (First smoke: drifts 0.5 m south down the floor's slope; the D box allows it.)

label: onto the threshing floor from the south and north to the long farmhouse's corner
why: up the yard bank's east end (top D 12.3) onto the floor, across it to just short of farmhouse_long's south-east corner (359.9-361.5, 15.7-18.1).

label: over the small bridge (S1.str.small_bridge_36365, S1.road.path_36380) W->E
why: the deck lands on bank_36060's top (368.8, 10.0-10.3) and on bank_36900 (375.3-375.4, 10.4-10.7) at H 0 (the frame's reading: the deck meets both bank tops level); the shore walls leave a gap of 1.1 m either side of the deck's centre line, the deck's hidden rails keep you on it. (Run 3, the S1 finisher: the east landing now at H -0.33 (the shore land held 0.7 m over the water 2.5 m in))

label: over the small bridge E->W
why: and back. (Run 3, the S1 finisher: the last legs due west off the deck's north half: the painted path's line off its south half (188 deg) meets the hollow's 35 deg face at (367.5, 9.96) and stalls the walker at X 367.2)

label: the bridge's south rail holds you (mid-deck, walking south)
why: from the deck's middle square to its south edge: the rail stops you on the deck (deck_s D 10.3 here; the kit's built width is a choice) and you stay at the deck's height, never in the stream (H -0.7).

label: the bridge's north rail holds you (mid-deck, walking north)
why: and to its north edge (deck_n D 10.97): the pool north of the bridge (to D 12.4) stays out of reach.

label: the corner at the bridge's west end (south side) doesn't lead into the stream
why: from the bank beside the deck's west end, south-east toward the water: the shore wall's gap (1.1 m either side of the deck's centre) is covered by the rails' run onto the bank (0.8 m); you stop on the bank. (Run 3, the S1 finisher: the north rail starts at X 368.1, so from this start south-east leads onto the deck, where the south rail holds the walker (369.7, 9.8, H -0.12): not into the stream)

label: the corner at the bridge's east end (south side) doesn't lead into the stream
why: from the east bank south-west toward the stream south of the deck's end (shore_n 376.3/10.5-377.4/10.2): stopped on the bank by the shore wall, the rail's run-on or elm_bare_36660's trunk (375.4, 9.6: mapped 1 m inside the stream's shore, see the report). (Run 3, the S1 finisher: the walker ends on the shore land inside the wall's loop round elm_bare_36660's roots (376.6, 9.3, H -0.43, the water at -0.7): stopped on land)

label: into the pale band from the terrace (S1.water.wash_band_34400: water, the lead's call): the shore stops you
why: down bank_33650's face (top D 4.1, foot = the band's north shore D 2.1 at X 338, H -0.7): the shore wall stops you about 0.35 m short of it.

label: into the stream from the bottom strip (its south shore stops you)
why: bank_south_34400 (top D -1.2 at X 368) to the stream's south shore (D 0.1 at X 368): stopped about 0.35 m short.

label: into the pool north of the bridge from its west bank, square to the shore (facing 315)
why: the pool's west shore runs (369.37, 10.94) -> (370.72, 12.27) (shore_n); square to it the walker stops 0.35 m short, at (370.05, 12.10), 1.6 m clear of the deck's centre line (outside the shore wall's gap at the bridge); the dyke above the pool is the charcoal train's lane, so the pool is reached from the west. (Walking east at 45 deg to this shore slides you along it and round its corner onto the north bank: no way into the water, seen in the first smoke run.) (Run 3, the S1 finisher: the shore land now runs down to the water, so the walker stops at the wall at the water's edge (370.4, 12.4, H -0.66), never below the water (-0.7))

label: into the stream past the road's east end (its north shore stops you)
why: east of the charcoal train's lane (its front driver walks to 384.9, 10.9): bank_36900's foot = the stream's north shore, D 10.6 at X 386.6 (its mapped top, D 9.9, lies south of its foot: the water at -0.7 maps 1 m north of a ground point): stopped about 0.35 m short.

why: the west edge runs from (267.21, -4.39) to (290.62, 30.54) (S2's east corners); 4.8 m square to it from the start, the walker stops 0.35 m short (radius + half the wall). With S2 joined the wall goes.

label: edge west (alone), north of the stall: the seam stops you (facing 146)
why: the same edge behind the stall, clear of its willows.

label: edge east: the silk's end stops you north of the stream (square to it, facing 326)
why: the east edge runs from (378.38, -4.39) to (401.79, 30.54); from above bank_37050 ESE down toward the edge at D ~13.7 (north of the stream's shore, D 10.8).

label: edge east: the silk's end stops you in the south-east corner, south of the stream (facing 326)
why: the bottom strip runs east past the stream's south shore's end (376.5, -0.22): the east wall must close it, and no water without a shore wall may lie in the way.

label: edge east: the silk's end stops you in the open north-east (facing 326)
why: blank silk, mist beyond: the wall must stand there too.

label: edge north: the silk's top stops you (facing 90)
why: the north edge D 30.54 (blank silk past the far fields): stop 0.35 m short.

label: edge north above the terraced fields: the silk's top stops you (facing 90)

label: edge south: the silk's bottom stops you under the willows (facing 270)
why: down bank_31700 (top D -0.75) and over bank_31825's line (D -2.9) to the bottom edge D -4.39: stop 0.35 m short.

label: edge south: the silk's bottom stops you below the farmsteads (facing 270)
why: the bottom strip south of the pale band, west of the stream.
